X Sues Bitcoin Influencers, Alleging Engagement Manipulation to Fraudulently Obtain at Least £207,384 in Creator Revenue X Internet Unlimited Company and X Corp. filed a lawsuit in the UK High Court on September 17 against Vivek Kumar Sen, Zamyang Sherpa, and operators of related accounts, alleging that they coordinated multiple X accounts to publish identical or substantially similar content, like and repost one another’s posts, artificially manipulate engagement metrics, and evade platform enforcement, fraudulently obtaining at least £207,384 from the Creator Revenue Sharing Program. X suspended the accounts on August 18 and is seeking the return of the funds, damages, interest, and legal costs. It also estimated that investigation, analysis, and remediation costs would total at least £75,000. — link

Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $6.21 Million in Weekly Net Inflows, While Spot Ethereum ETFs Post $140 Million in Net Outflows From September 14 to September 18 (ET), spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $6.21 million in net inflows, led by BlackRock’s IBIT with $121 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs posted $140 million in net outflows, ending four consecutive weeks of net inflows. — link

CoinGecko: Hyperliquid Ranks First Among Crypto Projects With $429 Million in Revenue This Year According to CoinGecko, the top 10 crypto projects by revenue from January 1 to September 15, 2026, were Hyperliquid with $429 million, Pumpfun with $322 million, Axiom Pro with $132 million, Sky with $130 million, GMGN with $126 million, Polymarket with $115 million, World Liberty Financial with $95.37 million, Paxos with $87.93 million, edgeX with $84.37 million, and Titan Builder with $83.47 million. The ranking excludes Tether, Circle, and Grayscale. — link

Bitcoin breaks above $85,000 as crypto liquidations hit $747 million According to Binance market data, Bitcoin surged above $85,000, reaching an intraday high of $85,299 before trading at $84,927, up 5.45% over the past 24 hours. CoinGlass data shows that total crypto liquidations reached $747 million over the past 24 hours, including $648 million in short positions and $98.78 million in longs. According to Lookonchain, as BTC broke above $85,000 and ETH surpassed $2,750, two short positions were liquidated. Trader 0x06bc’s short position of 5,867 ETH ($16.13 million) was partially liquidated, while trader 0xec0b’s short position of 122.88 BTC ($10.16 million) was fully liquidated. — link
